INTRODUCTION
This work is intended to supplement the 1909 edition of the Ken-
tucky Statutes . It contains all laws passed by the General Assembly
of Kentucky in 1910 , 1912 and 1914. All Acts which specifically
amend sections of the Kentucky Statutes are placed in numerical
order , with the proper section numbers . All new Acts which are
not amendments are placed under suitable headings and given appro-
priate numbers . Such sections of the Statutes as have been repealed
or affected by new laws are annotated so as to show this . Each
section has short subject headings at the beginning and a reference_
at the end to the book and page of the official Acts . It is hoped that
this latter feature will prove a great convenience .
This Supplement and the 1909 Statutes contain all the statute
law of Kentucky of a general character . By using the two books
together the old laws and the new can be brought together for the pur-
pose of comparison and the change in the old by the new readily
ascertained .
The notes, which cover all State and Federal cases decided between
the years 1908 and 1915 , have been compiled with great care and
with the purpose of stating fully the points decided in the cases , and
in many instances the facts on which the decisions rest . Also all the
cases from the old Kentucky Opinions involving statutes have been
cited . These notes apply to the Kentucky Statutes , the Acts in this
Supplement , and the Constitution of Kentucky , and embrace the valu-
able annotations of Charles B. Seymour , Esq ., of the Louisville Bar .
In an appendix are certain amendments to the Civil and Criminal
Codes , and certain personal Acts. There is also a table showing
where the various chapters of the Acts may be found in this volume ,
and an endeavor has been made to furnish a full Index .
Where the language of the sections of the Kentucky Statutes has
not been changed , neither the section nor its number has been given
unless the section has been annotated , then the section number is
printed with the notes underneath . The Supplement sections are anno-
tated beneath their text .
Numerous citations have been inserted to approved forms of instruc-
tions to be found in INSTRUCTIONS TO JURIES (KY. ) , ( Hobson , Blain
and Caldwell ) , and to various forms called for by the Statutes , given
in CALDWELL'S KENTUCKY FORM BOOK . This it is believed will give
an added value to the work as a book for frequent reference .
The Publisher .

SEC . 1 .
Statutes of 1909
Actions and Proceedings .
(1) The word " bitch " in an accusation does not come within this section . Craig
v. Pyles , 101 Ky . 593 , 18 R. 1043, 39 S. W. 33 ; Peters v. Garth , 20 R. 1934, 50 S. W. 682 .
(2 ) Malice does not mean or imply personal malice , but simply a wrongful act
done without just cause or excuse . Louisville Press Co. v . Tennelly , 105 Ky. 365 , 20
R. 1231, 49 S. W. 15.
(3) An insane delusion on the subject to which the slanderous words related is a
complete defense to the action under this section . Irvine v . Gibson , 117 Ky. 306 , 25
R. 1418, 77 S. W. 1106 .
SEC . 2 .
( 1) This section does not modify the common law rule that the relation of
master and servant or parent and child must appear . A mother can not recover for
the seduction of her illegitimate daughter without showing that she is under twenty-
one years of age . Taylor v. Daniel , 30 R. 377 , 98 S. W. 986 .
(2) For form of approved instruction under this section , with annotations , see
Instructions to Juries (Ky .) , Sec . 559 .
(3 ) For form of petition under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form No.
2980 .
SEC . 4.
( 1) An assault with an iron bar creates a cause of action under this section .
Morehead's Admx . v . Bittner , 106 Ky . 523 , 20 R. 1986 , 50 S. W. 857 .
(2) Where there is no widow or child left , the administrator can sue under this
section. The term "wrongful use of firearms " includes negligence . Howard's Admr .
v. Hunter , 126 Ky. 685 , 31 R. 1092, 104 S. W. 723 .
(3 ) The widow of one shot and killed by a marshal , liable on his bond under
K. S. 3690 , need not join the town or the commonwealth as plaintiff in suing the mar-
shal and his bondsmen. Bolton v . Ayers , 33 R. 591 , 110 S. W. 385 .
(4) The minor children have the right to be made parties plaintiff by their next
friend and the widow can not dismiss as to them without his consent . Martin v.
Smith , 33 R. 582 , 110 S. W. 413 .
( 5 ) The word "wrongful " in a petition under this section is broad enough to
include a careless , wanton , or malicious act . Young v . Young , 141 Ky. 76 , 132 S. W. 155.
( 6 ) A killing by a lunatic by the use of firearms was held to be within this
section as being wanton , although neither careless nor malicious . Young v. Young ,
141 Ky. 76 , 132 S. W. 155 .
(1)

SEC. 6. ACTIONS AND PROCEEDINGS .
(7) The limitation of one year applies to every action allowed for the death of a
person. Irwin v . Smith , 150 Ky. 147, 150 S. W. 22 .
(8) For form of petition under this section, see Kentucky Form Book , Forms Nos .
1168 , 1169 .
SEC . 6 .
This section gives a right of action against a Kentucky corporation for a death
caused by its negligence in navigating a vessel upon the high seas . South . Pac . Co. v.
De Valle da Costa , 190 Fed . 689 .
(Cir . Ct . App ., First Circuit, Oct. 4 , 1911. )
This right will be enforced in another jurisdiction where there is a like statute
and when no public policy is violated in the state where suit is brought . Ib .
This right of action and claim which is to be prosecuted by the personal repre-
sentative constitutes assets and is sufficient to uphold jurisdiction in probate court to
appoint an administrator to assert the liability and collect the claim even though
decedent was an alien . Ib. De Valle Da Costa v. South . Pac . Co. , March 16, 1908
(Cir . Ct. D. Mass . ) , 160 Fed . 216 .
De Valle Da Costa v. South . Pac . Co. , Feb. 17, 1909 (Cir . Ct . D. Mass . ) , 167 Fed .
654 , holds that limitation for the right of action under this section is one year even
in the foreign jurisdiction in which the suit is brought , citing Ky. Stats . 2516 .
( 1) L. & N. R. Co. v . Brown , 127 Ky. 732 , 32 R. 552 , 106 S. W. 795 ; Sturgess v.
Sturgess , 126 Ky . 80 , 31 R. 537 , 102 S. W. 884 ; Dudley v . I. C. R. Co. , 29 R. 1029, 96 S.
W. 835 , (K. S. Par . 10 ) ; I. C. R. Co. v . Sheegog , 126 Ky . 252 , 31 R. 691 , 103 S. W. 323 ;
L. & E. Mail Co. v . Barnes , 117 Ky . 860 , 25 R. 2036 , 79 S. W. 261 ; L. & N. R. Co. v.
Simrall's Admr ., 127 Ky. 55 , 31 R. 1269, 104 S. W. 1011 ; Gaines v . Johnson , 32 R. 58 ,
105 S. W. 281 .
(2 ) Under this section a recovery may be had for the death of a servant resulting
from the master's breach of contract to furnish a guard to protect him from assault by
others . Lewis ' Admr . v . Taylor Coal Co. , 112 Ky . 845 , 23 R. 2218 , 66 S. W. 1044.
(3 ) Under this section and Civil Code § 83 , where a horse and a driver are killed
by the same tort , the actions must be joined , although one recovery goes to the wife
and the other to the estate . The recovery for the death of the driver bars a subsequent
recovery for the horse. Cole's Admx . v. I. C. R. Co. , 120 Ky. 686, 27 R. 1087, 87 S. W.
1082 .
(4 ) Where the administrator conspires with the tort feasor to prevent an action
for wrongful death , the widow and children may sue . McLemore v. Sebree Coal &
Mining Co. , 121 Ky . 53 , 28 R. 25 , 88 S. W. 1062 .
( 5 ) The right to recovery under this section may be enforced by a suit of an
administrator , although the decedent was living without property or relatives in this
country . Trotta's Admr . v. Johnson , Briggs & Pitts , 121 Ky. 827 , 28 R. 851 , 90 S. W.
540 .
( 6 ) Where a railroad runs a defectively equipped train over an unsafe track at a
high rate of speed , killing a person , the question of punitive damages should be sub- .
mitted . I. C. R. Co. v. Sheegog's Admr ., 126 Ky. 252 , 31 R. 691 , 103 S. W. 323.
(7 ) To maintain the action created by this section , gross negligence need not be
shown . C. N. O. & T. P. Ry . Co. v. Evans ' Admr ., 129 Ky. 152, 110 S. W. 844 .
(8) In an action under this section for the death of an infant employed in a coal
mine in violation of the statutes , contributory negligence is a defense . Smith's Admr .
v. Natl . Coal & Iron Co. , 135 Ky. 671 , 117 S. W. 280 .
(9) Contributory negligence is a defense , but in case of death the plaintiff need not
prove the absence thereof . Warren's Admr . v. Jeunesse , Ky. 122, S. W. 862 .
( 10) A settlement by a decedent in his lifetime bars the right of action created
in his administrator by this section . Where the action for injuries suffered in the life-
time of the injured man survives , the widow and infant children can compel the prose-
cution of the action under this section by the administrator for their exclusive benefit
as against the claims of creditors . Lou . Ry . Co. v . Raymond's Admr ., 135 Ky . 738 , 123
S. W. 281 .
( 11 ) An action lies against a physician in favor of the personal representative
of a decedent , whose death resulted from the negligent failure of the physician to give

decedent proper treatment after he had undertaken the case .
Snyder , 139 Ky . 159, 129 S. W. 562 .
Randolph's Admr . v.
( 12) Upon the evidence in a certain case the Court was of opinion in this case
that no such gross negligence was shown as authorized punitive damages ; from this
conclusion one judge dissented . I. C. R. Co. v . Moss ' Admr ., 142 Ky . 658 , 134 S. W. 1122.
( 13) Where death results from injury by negligence and is not immediate , the
representatives of the deceased may , at their election , sue either for the pain and
suffering endured by deceased , or for his death ; they can not sue for both . C. & O.
Ry. Co. v. Banks ' Admr ., 142 Ky. 746 , 135 S. W. 285 .
( 14) In an action for the negligent killing of a person by a collision of boats on a
navigable river in Kentucky , the rules issued by the Secretary of War for regulating
the navigation of rivers are admissible in evidence . Johnson v. Westerfield's Admr .,
143 Ky. 10, 135 S. W. 425 .
( 15) An illegal sale of liquor to a person not made for the purpose of injuring him
nor with the knowledge that he intended to drink enough to produce injury or death ,
nor with reasonable grounds to believe that he could not be trusted with whisky , does
not give a cause of action under this section , although it caused the death of the party
to whom it was sold . Britton's Admr . v . Samuels , 143 Ky . 129, 136 S. W. 143.
( 16 ) The right of action under this section is vested .n the personal representative .
City of Louisville v . Hart's Admr ., 143 Ky. 171, 136 S. W. 212 .
( 17 ) Where one while intoxicated kills another , the merchant who sold the
intoxicating liquors is not civilly liable for the death . Waller's Admr . v. Collins-
worth , 144 Ky. 3 , 137 S. W. 766 .
( 18 ) The act of a railroad company in requiring its servants in charge of a
freight train engaged in interstate commerce to remain on duty for a longer time
than sixteen consecutive hours , in violation of the Federal Statute of March 4 , 1907
( U. S. Compiled Statute , Chapter 2939 , § 2 ) , was negligence per se ; inasmuch as
this negligence concurred with that of the engineer on the train in causing the death
of a brakeman on the train ; the personal representative of the brakeman who was
killed had a cause of action for death. St. L. , Iron Mt. & Sou . Ry. Co. v. McWhirter ,
Admx ., 145 Ky. 427 , 140 S. W. 672 ( reversed , 229 U. S. 265 ) .
( 19 ) The Commissioners of Sewerage of Louisville , a corporation , are not
civilly liable for a death occasioned by the tort or negligence of the agent or servant
of the corporation , in the performance of a duty which the corporation owed to the
public , and the doing of which was the exercise of power purely governmental . Smith's
Admr . v. Commissioners of Sewerage of Louisville , 146 Ky . 562 , 143 S. W. 3 .
( 20 ) In an action under this section , in which there was no evidence tending
to show recklessness or indifference to the safety of others , no instruction as to
punitive damages should have been given . Straight Creek Coal Co. v. Huddleston's
Admr ., 147 Ky. 94 , 143 S. W. 775 .
( 21 ) The limitation of one year applies to every action allowed for the death
of a person. Irwin v. Smith , 150 Ky . 147 , 150 S. W. 22 .
( 22 ) An action was brought in Kentucky under the law of Tennessee for
personal injuries sustained in Tennessee ; plaintiff died pending the action and the
action was revived in the name of his administrator . The widow was rightly per-
mitted to file a petition in said action for damages for the death of her husband and
to recover jointly with the administrator a judgment for the personal injuries and
the death . (Subsection 3. ) Proctor Coal Co. v. Beavers , 151 Ky . 839 , 152 S. W.
965 .
( 23 ) The right to recover damages for death caused in Tennessee by a wrong-
ful act in that state is controlled by the law of that state, although the main entry
of the mine in which the accident occurred is in Kentucky . Proctor Coal Co. v.
Beavers , 151 Ky. 839 , 152 S. W. 965 .
( 24 ) This statute is superseded by the Federal Employers ' Liability Law
(Act of April 22 , 1908 ) as to all cases within the Federal Statute . I. C. R. Co. v.
Doherty's Admr ., 153 Ky. 363 , 155 S. W. 1119 .
( 25 ) In an action under this section it is not necessary to allege that decedent
did not know of the danger or defect ; knowledge on decedent's part is a matter of
defense . L. & N. R. Co. v. Greenwell's Admr ., 155 Ky. 799 , 160 S. W. 479 .

SEC . 10. ACTIONS AND PROCEEDINGS .
(26 ) In a civil action to recover damages for death , an instruction was given to
find for defendant if he at the time of the killing believed and had reasonable grounds
to believe that his life was then in danger or that his person was then in danger of
violence at the hands of the deceased . Held , that this instruction was not prejudicial ,
although the phrase , " death or great bodily harm ," was to be preferred , it having
become thoroughly imbedded in the law of self -defense . Shields v. Neal , 158 Ky. 695 ,
166 S. W. 211 .
( 27 ) The measure of damages under the Federal Employers ' Liability Act is not
the same as under Ky. Stats . sec . 6. C. & O. Ry . Co. v . Dwyer's Admx ., 157 Ky . 590 ,
163 S. W. 752 .
(28 ) Action for death of brakeman
struction of Federal Hours of Service Act .
Co. , 158 Ky. 176 , 164 S. W. 818 .
dead -heading on interstate train . Con-
Osborne's Admr . v . C. N. O. & T. P. Ry.
( 29 ) For form of approved instruction under this section , with annotations , see
Instructions to Juries ( Ky. ) , Sec . 230 .
( 30 ) Grounds of Action .-Where a wife is killed by negligence or wrongful act ,
the husband can not recover damages for the loss of conjugal society except from
the time of the injury until her death . If no appreciable length of time elapsed after
the negligent act became operative until her death during which the husband could
have enjoyed the society of his wife , he can not recover for loss of conjugal society
and services . Rogers v. Fancy Farm Telephone Co. , 160 Ky . 841 .
( 31 ) For form of petition under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form
No. 1165 .
SEC . 7 .
( 1 ) It is an abuse of legal process to cause goods to be seized under a distress
warrant for rent not reserved in money . Grigsby's Exr . v. Ratecan , 6 Ky. Opinions ,
170 .
( 2 ) The remedy given a tenant by Code 653 is not exclusive . Board v. Luigart ,
150 Ky . 791 , 151 S. W. 9..
( 3 ) For form of approved instruction under this section , with annotations , see
Instructions to Juries (Ky. ) , Sec . 171 .
SEC. 8 .
( 1 ) A city is liable in damages for injury to property by a mob if the city
authorities have the ability to prevent the damages and have notice or good reason
to believe that a mob will destroy or attempt to destroy the property ; but no liability
attaches unless the city authorities have notice or good reason to believe that a
riotous assemblage is about to take place, or , after it has taken place, have notice
in time to prevent the injury . Tandy v. City of Hopkinsville , 160 Ky . 220 , 169 S. W.
703 .
The city is not liable to the owner of property who has contributed towards
inciting or inflaming the mob . Id .
SEC . 10 .
( 1 ) Myers v. Zoll , 119 Ky. 480 , 27 R. 167 , 84 S. W. 543 (K. S. Par . 1 ) ; Merrill
v. Puckett , 29 R. 595 , 93 S. W. 912 ( K. S. Par . 1 ) .
( 2 ) An action for the pain and suffering of a servant resulting from the
master's breach of contract to furnish a guard to protect him from an assault does
not survive the death of the servant . Lewis ' Admr . v. Taylor Coal Co. , 112 Ky . 845 ,
23 R. 2218 , 66 S. W. 1044 .
(3) Where a resident of Indiana is there injured and sues for damages in
Kentucky , and dies pending the action , the survival is governed by the Kentucky , and
not the Indiana , statutes . Austin's Admr . v. P. C. C. & St. L. Ry. Co. , 122 Ky. 304 ,
28 R. 1235 , 91 S. W. 742 .
4

ACTIONS AND PROCEEDINGS . SEC . 11 .
( 4 ) An appeal in an election contest abates when the contestee dies pending
his appeal , no survival being provided in this section . Galvin v . Shafer , 130 Ky . 563 ,
113 S. W. 485 .
(5) An action for damages for permissive waste survives . Prescott's Admr . v .
Grimes , 143 Ky. 191, 136 S. W. 206 .
(6) A judgment in an action for assault and battery was reversed ; pending the
appeal the defendant died . On the return of the case the petition was dismissed , as
the right of action did not survive . Shield's Admr . v. Rowland , 151 Ky. 822 , 152
S. W. 943 .
SEC. 11 .
A plaintiff having both possession and the legal title of land may bring suit to
quiet title in the state court against the trustee in bankruptcy of plaintiff's grantor .
The state court having first entertained may hold jurisdiction . Davis v . Planters
Trust Co. , et al., Walter Evans , J. , 196 Fed . 970 .
( 1) Sheffield v . Day , 28 R. 754 , 90 S. W. 545 ; Engle v. Tennis Coal Co. , 125
Ky. 239 , 30 R. 1269 , 101 S. W. 309 ; Brown v. Ward, 32 R. 261 , 105 S. W. 964 .
( 2 ) In an action under this section , it must be alleged that plaintiff is the owner
and in possession of the land . Goff v. Lowe , 25 R. 2176 , 80 S. W. 219 ; Floyd v .
L. & . N. R. Co. , 25 R. 2147 , 80 S. W. 204 ; Dupoyster v . Turk , 33 R. 320 , 110 S. W. 260 ;
Dupoyster v. Dunn , 113 S. W. 880 ; Cockrell v . Colson , 116 S. W. 775 .
(3 ) An action under this section is properly in equity , although all the issues
are legal . Chenault v . Eastern Ky. Timber & Lumber Co. , 119 Ky . 170 , 26 R. 1078 ,
83 S. W. 552 .
(4 ) Where a deed of a mineral right claimed by the plaintiff was on record
before the defendants acquired any title to the land and where defendants attempted
to convert such mineral right to their own use , plaintiff need not show possession of
the land to justify an action under this section. Eversole v . Va . Iron , Coal & Coke
Co. , 122 Ky . 649 , 29 R. 151, 92 S. W. 593 ; Fox v . Cornett , 29 R. 246 , 92 S. W. 959 .
(5) An action to set aside a fraudulent deed as a cloud upon the title is not an
action within this section and possession is not necessary to authorize the action .
Cawood v. Howard , 113 S. W. 109 .
( 6 ) The possession must be shown at the commencement of the action , if it is
denied . Horn v . Bates , 114 S. W. 763 .
(7 ) This action must be brought in the county where the land or some part of
it lies . Daniel v. New Era Land Co. , 137 Ky. 535 , 126 S. W. 108 .
( 8 ) Where the petition admitted that the railroad had obstructed a part of
the land claimed with a fence , this was an admission that the railroad was in posses-
sion ; and the petition did not state a cause of action under this section. L. & N.
R. Co. v. Taylor , 138 Ky. 437 , 128 S. W. 325 .
(9) An action to quiet title does not lie in favor of one having no title. Deaton v .
Burton , 142 Ky. 7, 133 S. W. 958 .
( 10 ) This action will not lie against a person in the actual possession of land .
Newsome v. Hamilton , 142 Ky. 5, 133 S. W. 952 .
( 11 ) In an action to quiet title it appeared that the plaintiff had conveyed to
the defendant with warranty the land in controversy . The action was properly dis-
missed. A verbal agreement of defendant to reconvey was not enforcible . Blevins v.
Blevins , 143 Ky. 220 , 136 S. W. 195 .
( 12 ) In an action to enforce a lien on land , the plaintiff made a third party a
defendant , alleging that he was claiming the land without right ; this defendant made
default . A sale under a judgment in that action barred the claim of the defendants
thereto . Barnett v . Bauer Cooperage Co. , 145 Ky . 163 , 140 S. W. 146 .
( 13 ) A judgment by default quieting title can not be attacked collaterally ,
although the party so attacking it was in possession at the time the action to quiet
title was instituted . Barnett v . Bauer Cooperage Co. , 145 Ky . 163 , 140 S. W. 146 .
( 14 ) In this action it was held that a plaintiff had failed to establish his title .
Slone v. Hall , 145 Ky. 232 , 140 S. W. 188 .

SEC . 12a . ACTIONS AND PROCEEDINGS .
( 15 ) A suit may be maintained under this section upon a title acquired by
fifteen years ' adverse possession ; in order for a trespasser to obtain such title beyond
his actual close he must have some well defined or well marked boundary showing the
extent of his claim ; and the mere fact that he erroneously thought that his deed
embraced land not embraced therein will not of itself extend his adverse holding beyond
the boundaries of his deed . LeMoyne v . Hays , 145 Ky . 415 , 140 S. W. 552 .
( 16 ) To dispossess a rightful owner , the disseisor must so occupy , use and
control the land , that his possession and claim are notorious , and are such as to make
impossible during their existence a similar occupancy , use and control of the same
land by the owner . Le Moyne v. Hays , 145 Ky . 415 , 140 S. W. 552 .
( 17 ) In an action to quiet title, defendant denied the title and the possession
of plaintiff and pleaded title in himself ; upon plaintiff's failure to prove title the
petition was properly dismissed . The evidence tending to show plaintiff's title is set
out in the opinion . Musick v. Horn , 145 Ky . 639 , 140 S. W. 1014 .
( 18 ) In an action to quiet title, the petition showed that the plaintiffs were
not in actual possession of the land ; by an amendment they prayed for the recovery
of the possession of the land and damages ; a judgment in their favor was not erroneous .
Nugent & Stansberry v . Mallory, 145 Ky. 824 , 141 S. W. 850 .
( 19 ) In an action to quiet title , a judgment by default awarding the property
to plaintiff was sustained . Martin v . Ky. Lands Investment Co. , 146 Ky . 525 , 142
S. W. 1038 .
( 20 ) In an action under this section plaintiff must make and sustain an allega-
tion of possession . City of Cloverport v . Polk Canning Co. , 149 Ky . 414 , 149 S. W. 817 .
( 21 ) In an action to quiet title the defendant set up the boundary which he
claimed and prayed that his title be quieted . The court had a right to settle the
whole controversy , although the plaintiff did not show that he was in possession .
Hall v. Hall , 149 Ky . 817 , 149 S. W. 1128 .
( 22 ) In this action upon the facts it was error to dismiss the petition . Cont .
Realty Co. v. Harvey , 151 Ky. 703 , 152 S. W. 755 .
(23 ) A judgment under this section was reversed and the case remanded with
directions to give the parties an opportunity to take further proof . Clark's Heirs v .
Boyd , 152 Ky. 234 , 153 S. W. 227 .
( 24 ) The owner of mineral rights may sue the owner of the surface who claims
under a deed purporting to convey to him the absolute fee simple title , to cancel such
deed in so far as it purports to convey the minerals which had theretofore been severed
by conveyance of the remote common grantor , and to quiet his title, without alleging
actual possession of the minerals . Kentenia Corporation v . Boreing Land and Mining
Co. , 159 Ky. 61 , 166 S. W. 780 .
(25 ) Where plaintiff claims under one patent and defendant under a deed from
the patentee of another patent , plaintiff, if not in possession , can not maintain an
action to cancel the deed under which defendant claims and to quiet his title thereto ,
without showing some equitable ground for its cancellation other than the mere fact
that it covers the lands in controversy and thereby creates a cloud on plaintiff's title .
Cumberland Company v . Kelly , 156 Ky. 397 , 160 S. W. 1077 .

ants . Be it further enacted , That to carry out the provisions of this

bandry of the Kentucky Experiment Station , ex - officio member , and four

duties . There shall also be a County Live Stock Inspector appointed

Court of each county for which he is appointed . The Fiscal Court of

graduated veterinarian when such is available , otherwise , an experienced

mals . Said State Live Stock Sanitary Board shall, within thirty days

term of four (4 ) years , and until his successor has been elected and

Live Stock Sanitary Board , which in any event shall not exceed the

Capitol , at Frankfort , Kentucky , or at the Kentucky Experiment Station

services other than the compensation allowed him by the State Live
Stock Sanitary Board , and he shall be subject to removal from office.
by said Board any time for cause . Should assistants be deemed neces-
sary at any time same may be employed to be paid not over five ( $5.00 )
dollars per day and all necessary traveling expenses while in the dis-

such duties . [ Acts 1914 , p . 385. ]

2. Infectious or contagious diseases-duty of Board-officers . That
whenever any contagious or infectious disease in live stock shall exist
in the State , it shall be the duty of the State Live Stock Sanitary Board
promptly to take steps to suppress and prevent the spread of the same ;
and said board , in its direction [ discretion ] shall have authority to issue
its proclamation that such disease exists in any county or counties , and warn
all persons to isolate all animals affected by such disease , or which may
have been exposed thereto , give instructions as to the precautions to
be taken to prevent the spread of such disease ; to order any farms or
parts thereof put in quarantine at the owner's expense , in the event
said owner has not complied with the provisions of this Act , and pre-
scribe the regulations therefor ; to order the destruction or proper dis-
posal of the carcasses of animals dead or incurable from such disease ,
and to prescribe regulations for the cleaning and disinfecting of prem-
ises , buildings , stockyards , railway stations , cars , and other places or
objects which may have been exposed to infection . The Kentucky Ex-
periment Station shall co -operate with the State Live Stock Sanitary
Board , and the said State Live Stock Sanitary Board shall co - operate
with the Kentucky Experiment Station , in quarantining and controlling
the movement of hogs affected by this disease or exposed to same .
It shall be the duty of the State Experiment Station , upon the request
of the State Live Stock Sanitary Board or the State Veterinarian , to
make such bacteriological and pathological examination as may be
deemed necessary . [ Acts 1914 , p . 386. ]

an annual report to the Governor of its doings and expenditures under
this Act . [ Acts 1914 , p . 387. ]

Bureau of Animal Industry of the United States Government , the Ken-
tucky Experiment Station or the State Live Stock Sanitary Board . Any

in consideration that he is to have an agreed portion of the recovery applied on

(4 ) An attorney may be liable on a contract for assistance rendered him in
preparing a case ; but if the contract be contingent on success it will not be en-
forcible . Lynn v. Moss , 139 Ky . 637, 23 R. 214 , 62 S. W. 712 .
SEC . 210 .
( 1) The use of a private passway is not adverse to the possession of the servient
estate within this section . Hegan v . Pendennis Club , 23 R. 861 , 64 S. W. 464 .
(2 ) A vendor conveyed and warranted certain land , to a part of which he had
no title , and which part was adversely held by another ; vendor afterwards acquired
title to such part . This after - acquired title , did not inure to the benefit of the
purchaser . The attempted conveyance and warranty was void , and invested the pur-
chaser with no rights . Altemus v. Nichols , 115 Ky . 506 , 24 R. 2401 , 74 S. W. 221 .
(3 ) Under this section the possession must be actual , and such as would imply
that the tenant holds against all the world , and will acquire title if maintained
long enough. In this case , the person holding was in possession through tenants ,
whose lease directed them to farm the whole tract . They farmed only a part to
which the owner had good title , but did not farm that portion to which adverse
possession was claimed , and did nothing to direct anyone's attention to such un-
farmed tract . It was held that this unfarmed portion was not held in adverse pos-
session by the landlord . Interstate Investment Co. v. Bailey , 29 R. 468 , 93 S. W. 578 .
(4 ) A plaintiff can not avail himself of this section if the question whether his
possession was adverse , was in issue in the action and was decided against him .
Westerfield v. McDonald , 30 R. 1034 , 100 S. W. 230 .
(5) This section is not in conflict with Civil Code , Section 439 , allowing right
of discovery on return of "no property found ." Bramblett v. Couch , 32 R. 311 , 105
S. W. 460 .
(6 ) A claim to land in adverse possession may be disposed of by will . Preston
v. Woolly, 5 Ky. Opinions , 511 .
(7) Two adjoining lots were sold at an auction to different persons ; one pur-
chaser erected a fence beyond the boundary line ; the conveyance by the original
vendor to the second purchaser was not champertous . Perciful v. Coleman , 24 R.
1685, 72 S. W. 29 .
( 8) An infant conveyed land ; his grantee took possession ; a conveyance of
the land to another person by the first grantor upon coming of age was not cham-
pertous . Smith v . Cornett , 124 Ky. 63, 30 R. 302 , 98 S. W. 297 .
(9) After confirmation of a judicial sale a sale by the purchaser before obtain-
ing possession from the defendant was not champertous by reason of the posses-
sion of the defendant pending a writ of possession . Bartley v . Redmon's Admx ., 115
S. W. 831 .
( 10) The fact that a claimant lived on land sold under a judicial sale in an action
to which the claimant was not a party does not make the sale champertous . Martin
v. Turner , 115 S. W. 833 .
( 11 ) A deed to land which was in the adverse possession of another at the
time of the making of the deed is void ; a correspondence between certain parties
before adverse possession was taken was held not to take the case out of this rule .
Tool v. Kinman , 140 Ky . 208 , 130 S. W. 1073.
( 12) The holding of a grantee of a life estate which has been set apart to a
widow as dower , is not adverse to the title of the remainderman ; a conveyance by
the remainderman is not champertous by reason of such possession . Ison v . Cornett ,
141 Ky. 771 , 133 S. W. 756 .
( 13) Possession held adversely under an oral contract for the purchase of land
was adverse within this section . Muncy v. Smith , 142 Ky . 201 , 133 S. W. 1152 .
( 14) Certain possession was held not adverse within this section . Perry v.
Veal , 142 Ky . 441 , 134 S. W. 458 .
( 15 ) A conveyance made in pursuance of an oral contract which was entered
into when there was no adverse possession of the land is not within this section ,

SEC . 331A.
CHILD LABOR LAW.
AN ACT to regulate the labor and employment of children and minors and to make
the provisions thereof effective .
[ Act March 21 , 1914. Acts 1914 , Chap . 72 , p . 212. ]
Repealing clause . That an Act entitled " An Act to regulate child
labor and to make the provisions thereof effective , " approved March
18 , 1908 (which Act constitutes Section 331A , of the Kentucky Statutes
of 1909 ) , and an Act entitled " An Act to amend an Act entitled ' An Act
to regulate child labor and to make the provisions thereof effective , ap-
proved March 18 , 1908 , ' approved March 25 , 1910 , " be and the same are
hereby repealed ; and the following sections are hereby enacted in lieu
thereof and shall constitute Section 331A of the Kentucky Statutes :
SEC. 331A .
1. Child labor unlawful to employ children under fourteen in cer-
tain employments —or in any business in school term . No child under
fourteen years of age shall be employed , permitted or suffered to work
in or in connection with any factory , mill , workshop , mercantile estab-
lishment , store , office , printing establishment , bakery, laundry , restaurant ,
hotel , apartment house , theater , motion picture establishment , or in the
distribution or transmission of merchandise or messages . It shall be un-
lawful for any person , firm , or corporation to employ any child under
fourteen years of age in any in business or service whatever during any
part of the term during which the public schools of the district in which
the child resides are in session . Nor shall any child under fourteen
years of age be permitted to perform in or appear upon the stage of
any theater , motion picture establishment or other place of public amuse-
ment , whether for pay or not . [Acts 1914 , p . 212. ]
See notes to cases construing this law, following subsection 17.
SEC . 331A .
2. Conditions of employment between fourteen and sixteen -certifi-
cate-labor inspector -his duties -authority . No child between fourteen
and sixteen years of age shall be employed , permitted or suffered to
work in or in connection with any factory , mill , workshop , mercantile
establishment , store , office , printing establishment , bakery , laundry , res-

SEC . 331A . CHILDREN .
taurant , hotel , apartment house , theater, motion picture establishment ,
or in the distribution or transmission of merchandise or messages , un-
less the person , firm or corporation employing him procures from the
local school authorities and keeps on file and accessible to the truant
officers and to the labor inspectors , an employment certificate as here-
inafter prescribed , and keeps two complete lists of all such children em-
ployed therein, one on file and one conspicuously posted near the prin-
cipal entrance of the building in which such children are employed . On
termination of the employment of a child so registered , and whose cer-
tificate is so filed , such certificate shall be returned by the employer to
the officer by whom it was issued within two days of the termination
of the employment of such child . A labor inspector may make demand
on an employer in whose establishment a child apparently under the
age of sixteen years is employed or permitted or suffered to work and
whose employment certificate is not then filed as required by this Act ,
that such employer shall either furnish him, within ten days , evidence
satisfactory to him that such child is in fact sixteen years of age or over ,
or shall cease to employ , or permit , or suffer such child to work therein .
A labor inspector may require from such employer the same evidence of
age of such child as is required for the issuance of an employment cer-
tificate , and the employer furnishing such evidence shall not be required
to furnish any further evidence of the age of the child . In case such
employer shall fail to produce and deliver to the labor inspector , within
ten days after such demand , such evidence of the age therein required
of him , and thereafter continue to employ such child , or permit or suffer
such child to work in such establishment , proof of the giving of such
notice and of such failure to produce and file such evidence shall be
prima facie evidence in any prosecution brought for violation of the pro-
vision that such child is under sixteen years of age and is unlawfully em-
ployed . [ Acts 1914 , p. 213. ]
SEC . 331A .
3. By whom employment certificates issued . Employment certificates
shall be issued only by the superintendent of schools or by a person
authorized by him in writing , acting in his name. Where there is no
local superintendent of schools they shall be issued by the county super-
intendent of schools , or by a person so authorized by him. [ Acts 1914 ,
p. 214. ]

as provided hereinafter . ( 2 ) A duly attested transcript of the birth

of recording births ; or a passport , or a duly attested transcript of a
certificate of baptism showing the date of birth and place of baptism of

SEC. 331A .
10. Safeguards and safety appliances required where infants are em-
ployed . It shall be the duty of the owner of any manufacturing estab-
lishment where any person under twenty -one years of age is employed ,
his agents , superintendents or other persons in charge of same , to fur-
nish and supply, when practicable , or cause to be furnished and supplied
to him, belt shifters or other safe mechanical contrivance for the pur-
pose of throwing belts on or off pulleys ; and , whenever practicable ,
machinery therein shall be provided with loose belts . All vats , pans ,
saws , planes , cogs , gearings , belting , set screws and machinery of every
description which is palpably dangerous , shall be properly guarded and
no person shall remove or make ineffective any safeguard around or
attached to any such appliances or machinery, while the same is in
use, unless for the purpose of immediately making repairs thereto , and
all such safeguards shall be promptly replaced . No person under
eighteen years of age shall be allowed to clean machinery while it is
in motion . [Acts 1914 , p. 221. ]
SEC . 331A .
11. Infants not to be employed in first , second or third class cities
as messengers of company before six a . m. or after nine p . m. In cities
of the first , second or third class , no person under the age of twenty -one
years shall be employed , permitted or suffered to work as a messenger
for any telegraph, telephone or messenger company in the distribution ,
transmission or delivery of goods or messages before six o'clock in
the morning or after nine o'clock in the evening of any day . [ Acts
1914 , p . 221. ]

SEC . 331A .
12. Females under twenty -one not to work requiring constant stand-
ing . No female under twenty- one years of age shall be employed , per-
mitted or suffered to work in any capacity in this Commonwealth ,
where such work compels her to remain standing constantly . [ Acts
1914 , p . 222. ]
SEC . 331A .
13. Lime -washed or painted walls required . The walls and ceiling
of each room in every manufacturing establishment where minors are
employed shall be lime -washed or painted when , in the opinion of the
labor inspector , it shall be conducive to the health or cleanliness of
the persons working therein . [ Acts 1914 , p .. 222. ]
SEC . 331A .
14. Copy of act to be posted . A copy of this Act shall be conspicu-
ously posted and kept in each workroom of every mill , mine , workshop ,
theater , bowling alley, laundry or public messenger company , and manu-
facturing , mercantile or printing establishment in this Commonwealth .
[ Acts 1914 , p . 222. ]
SEC . 331A .
15. As to certain street employments - boys-girls -restrictions and
prohibitions-certificates , badges- delinquents -persons abetting - viola-
tions fined -penalties . No boy under fourteen years of age , nor girl
under eighteen years of age shall be employed , permitted or suffered
to work at any time in any city of the first , second or third class in or
in connection with the street occupations of peddling , boot -blacking ,
the distribution or sale of newspapers , magazines , periodicals or circu-
lars , nor in any other occupation pursued in any street or public place .
No boy between fourteen and sixteen years of age shall be employed ,
permitted or suffered to work in any city of the first , second or third
class in or in connection with the street occupations of peddling , boot-
blacking , the distribution or sale of magazines , periodicals or circulars ,
nor in any other occupation pursued in any street or public place except
upon the following conditions :
(A) Boys between fourteen and sixteen years of age shall , upon
application to the school authorities , as in the case of an employment
certificate , and upon compliance with all of the requirements for the
issuance of an employment certificate , be entitled to receive from the
officer authorized to issue employment certificates a badge , which shall
authorize the recipient to engage in the trades or occupations above
mentioned between the hours of six o'clock A. M. and eight P. M. of
each day , but at no other time . Such badge shall be displayed con-
spicuously by the recipient while so engaged and shall be renewed
annually on the first day of January . The color of all such badges issued
in the same calendar year shall be the same and said color shall be
changed each year upon renewal .

(B ) Boys between fourteen and sixteen years of age who comply
with all of the requirements for the issuance of an employment certifi-
cate except the educational requirement (that is, the filing of a school
record or the passing of an examination in lieu thereof ) shall be en-
titled to receive from the officer authorized to issue employment cer-
tificates a badge which shall authorize the recipient to engage in the
above mentioned trades or occupations at such time or times between
six A. M. and eight P. M. in each day as the public school of the city
or district where such boy resides are not in session , but at no other
time . All such badges issued in the same calendar year shall be of
the same color ; but in either form , design , or color shall be so different
from the badges issued to boys who comply with the educational re-
quirements above mentioned as to be readily distinguishable therefrom.
Such badges shall be renewed annually upon the first of January , and
their color shall be changed each year upon renewal .
Any child who shall engage in any such street occupation in viola-
tion of any of the provisions of this section shall be deemed delinquent
and shall be brought before any court or magistrate having jurisdic-
tion over juvenile delinquents , and shall be dealt with according to
law . The labor inspectors , truant officers , police officers , and juvenile
court probation officers shall enforce the provisions of this section . Who-
ever furnishes or sells to any minor any article of any description with
the knowledge that said minor intends to sell said article in violation
of the provisions of this section , or who shall continue to furnish or
sell articles of any description to a minor after having received written
notice from any officer charged with the enforcement of this section ,
or from the officer issuing the badge required as aforesaid , that said
minor is unlicensed to sell such article , shall be punished by a fine of
not less than fifteen dollars nor more than one hundred dollars for
each offense . [ Acts 1914 , p . 222. ]
SEC . 331A .
16. Violations and penalties parents — employers corporations—
fines . Whoever employs or suffers or permits a child under sixteen
years of age to work , and any parent, guardian or any adult person
under whose care or control a child under such age is , who suffers
or permits such child to work , in violation of any of the provisions
of this Act , shall be punished for the first offense by a fine of not less
than fifteen dollars nor more than fifty dollars ; for a second offense
by a fine of not less than fifteen dollars nor more than one hundred
dollars , or by imprisonment for not more than thirty days , or by both
such fine and imprisonment ; for a third or any subsequent offense by
a fine of not less than two hundred dollars , or by imprisonment for
not less than thirty days , or by both such fine and imprisonment . Who-
ever continues to employ any child in violation of any of the provisions
of this Act after having been notified thereof in writing by a truant
officer , a labor inspector or other authorized officer , shall , for every
day thereafter that such employment continues , be fined not less than
five nor more than twenty dollars . A failure to produce to a truant
officer or labor inspector any employment certificate or list required
by this Act shall be prima facie evidence of the illegal employment of
any person whose employment certificate is not produced , or whose

Any person , firm or corporation who hinders or delays any labor

which will directly tend to prevent such state of dependency , neglect
or delinquency , or to remove the conditions which render such child
either a neglected , dependent or delinquent child , as aforesaid , shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and , on conviction thereof, shall

6. Who may receive pensions . That any indigent , disabled per-
son who has been an actual bona fide resident of this State con-
tinuously since January 1 , 1907 , and who did actual military service
in the Confederate Army from the date of his enlistment till the close
of the war , or until he was honorably discharged , as an officer or private
soldier or sailor in the military or naval service of the Confederate States
of America , in the war of 1861-5 , or the widow of such officer or private
soldier or sailor to whom she was married prior to January 1 , 1890 ,
and who was living with him as his lawful wife at the time of his death
shall be paid out of the State Treasury the sum of ten dollars per month
upon proof of the fact according to forms and regulations prescribed
by this Act and conditions prescribed therein ; Provided , that any officer
or private soldier or sailor who was prevented from so serving till the
close of the war , or until he was honorably discharged by reason of
wounds received or disease contracted in line of duty , which rendered
him unable to perform further military service , shall be entitled to the
bnefits of this Act as though he had served until the close of the war

or private soldier or sailor who deserted or was dishonorably discharged ,
shall not be entitled to the benefits of this Act unless he re - enlisted
or returned to the service in the Confederate army and served until the
close of the war or until he was honorably discharged or was prevented
from so serving by wounds received or disease contracted in line of
duty which rendered him unable to perform further military service .

of the war , to take the oath of allegiance to the United States Govern-

such oath , such soldier shall not be adjudged a deserter , but he shall

or as if he had taken such oath of allegiance at the close of the war .

SEC . 445b .
Constitutional Amendment .
CONVICT LABOR .
AN ACT to amend the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky by allowing
the employment of convict labor upon public roads and bridges and State farms .
1. Convict labor-employed on public roads . That Section 253 of
the Constitution of this State be amended so that the Commonwealth of
Kentucky may use and employ outside of the walls of the penitentiaries
in such manner and means as may be provided by law, persons con-
victed of felony and sentenced to confinement in the penitentiary for
the purpose of constructing , or reconstructing and maintaining public
roads and public bridges or for the purpose of making and preparing
material for public roads and bridges and that the Commonwealth of
Kentucky may , by the use and employment of convict labor outside of
the walls of the penitentiary by other ways or means , as may be pro-
vided by law , aid the counties for road and bridge purposes , work on
the State farm or farms .
2. To be voted on . This amendment shall be submitted to the voters
of the State for their ratification or rejection at the time and in the
manner provided for under Section 256 of the Constitution of Ken-
tucky , and under the provisions of the Act of May 12 , 1897 , same being
Section 1459 of the compilation of laws known as designate as Carroll's
1913 edition of Kentucky Statutes . [ Acts 1914 , Chap . 93 , p . 496. ]
Consult in connection with this act Const . Sec . 253 , Ky. Stats . Secs . 3807-3811 .

The General Assembly shall have power to divide property into
classes and to determine what class or classes of property shall be

Any law passed or enacted by the General Assembly pursuant to

last preceding the filing of any petition shall be the basis upon which

nine hundred and seventeen . After that time, the power of the refer-
endum may be ordered either by the petition signed by five per cent .
of the legal voters or by the Legislative Assembly at the time said
acts or bills are enacted . The General Assembly enacting the bill shall
provide a way by which the act shall be submitted to the people . The
filing of a referendum petition against one or more items , sections or
parts of an Act shall not delay the remainder of that Act from becom-
ing operative .

their ratification or rejection at the time and in the manner provided for
under Section 256 of the Constitution of Kentucky , and under Section

EXHUMATION OF BODIES .
SEC . 532a .
AN ACT entitled an act to authorize the investigation and exhumation of anybody
whose death resulted from suspected poisoning , or other illegal cause
unknown , and the employment of competent medical assistance in determining
the same .
Exhumation of bodies-duty of coroner -County Judge or justice-
fee-chemist . That it is hereby made the duty of any coroner , County
Judge , or justice of the peace , upon the receipt of an affidavit from any
person or persons stating that they believe and have reasonable grounds
to believe that any person who is dead and buried , died from poisoning ,
or other illegal cause unknown , to have the body of said dead person
exhumed , and have the proper chemical or other examination made of
said body in order to determine the cause of death .
When , in the opinion of the officer holding the inquest , it shall be
necessary to have a post mortem examination of the body of said dead
person made during said inquest , he shall employ a competent surgeon
or physician for that purpose , and if said officer suspects poisoning he
shall employ a competent chemist to analyze the body , or any part thereof .
It shall be the duty of said officer and his employees , immediately
after said inquest proceedings have been held and concluded , to make
out , sign and file , in the office of the County Court Clerk of the county
in which such investigation was begun , a written and sworn report em-
bracing concisely and fully their findings . The surgeon or physicians so
employed and the chemist shall each be allowed for their services a
reasonable fee , to be fixed by the Fiscal Court and paid out of the county
levy , and upon their failure to file their report as herein specified , they
shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor , and upon conviction be fined in
any sum not less than one hundred nor more than five hundred dollars ,
and the officer so directing and conducting said investigation , or inquest
shall, in like manner , receive per diem , as compensation for his services ,
the maximum fee prescribed by law for services required of and rendered
by him by virtue of the office he holds , and should he fail to file his
report as herein specified , he shall be subject, upon conviction , to the
maximum penalties prescribed by law for failure to perform the duties
of his office .
All acts and parts of acts in conflict herewith are hereby repealed .
Whereas , there is a great prevalency of poisoning and other illegal
taking of human life , there is , therefore , an emergency declared to exist ,
and this Act shall take effect from and after its passage .
[Act March 13 , 1912. Acts 1912 , Chap . 63 , p . 217. ]
This act seems to take the place of Sec . 532 Ky. Stats ., except the last sentence
of 532 to -wit : All the expenses of an inquest held in a city of over thirty thousand
inhabitants shall be paid by such city .

SEC . 564. [ As amended . ]
Stock may be converted into bonds , etc.-may be increased - preferred
or common . Any corporation organized under this law may divide its
shares into classes , such as preferred , common and deferred shares , or
as may be otherwise designated , and it may give to each of the several
classes such priority of right in the payment of the dividends , and in

that the holders of its preferred stock shall be entitled , upon terms pre-
scribed by it, to convert the same into the bonds or other obligations of
the corporation . No preferred stock shall be issued except for cash or
its equivalent , nor for less than the par value of the shares , which shall
be stated in the certificates representing the preferred and common stock
respectively . Any such corporation , all of whose outstanding stock is
common stock may , by a resolution adopted by the vote of the holders
of not less than two-thirds in amount of its outstanding captial stock ,
cast in person or by proxy , at a special meeting of stockholders called
for the purpose and of which notice shall have been given as provided in
the by-laws of the company , at least twenty days before the date of the
meeting , or at the annual meeting of the stockholders of the company , or
by the written consent of the holders of not less than two -thirds in
amount of its capital stock , distribute or convert its outstanding capital
stock into preferred and common stock in such proportion as shall be
fixed by such resolution or written consent : Provided , that all holders of
stock of the company at the time of such distribution shall be entitled to
the same pro rata proportions of such preferred and common stock . And
by a resolution adopted by the like vote or by such written consent ,
the capital stock of any corporation may be increased and the increased
stock may be common or preferred stock , or partly one and partly the
other , as may be fixed by such resolution or written consent . Any such
preferred stock hereinbefore referred to shall be entitled to receive quar-
terly, semi -annual or annual dividends thereon at such rate as may be
prescribed by the resolution or written consent under which the same was
issued , and such dividends shall be payable as provided in the said
resolution or written consent , before any dividends shall be declared on
the common stock ; and on the dissolution of the company , voluntary or
otherwise , the holders of preferred stock shall be entitled to have their
shares redeemed at par before any distribution of any part of the assets
of the company shall be made to the holders of the common stock .

SEC . 576a .
SALE OF ASSETS OF CORPORATION WHOSE CHARTER WILL
SOON EXPIRE .
AN ACT to provide for the sale and purchase of the assets of a corporation created
under the laws of this Commonwealth , whose charter will expire within two
years from the date of such sale and purchase .
[ Act March 11, 1912. Acts 1912 , Chap . 31 , p . 147. ]
1. Authorizing corporations to sell entire assets to like corporations-
consent of three -fourths of stock required . Any corporation organized
under the laws of this Commonwealth may , at any time within two years
before the expiration of such charter , sell and convey to any other cor-
poration organized under the laws of this Commonwealth and engaged
in the same character of business , all of its property , rights , privileges ,
franchises , easements , rights of way , and all other property and property
rights it may use or possess , to such other corporation , upon such terms
and conditions as may be agreed to in writing by three - fourths in amount
of the stockholders of the selling corporation . [ Acts 1912 , p . 147. ]
SEC . 576b .
Same character of corporation may buy-three-fourths of stock .
Any corporation organized under the laws of this Commonwealth is hereby
authorized to purchase the corporate assets of any corporation organized
under the laws of this Commonwealth and engaged in the same character
of business , upon such terms as may be agreed to in writing by three-
fourths in amount of its stockholders , and from and after purchase and
sale the purchasing corporation shall be vested with all the rights , privi-
leges , franchises , easements , rights of way and all other property and
assets of the selling corporation , and be liable for all the obligations of
the selling corporation , in the same manner and with like effect as if
such corporations had been formally consolidated under the laws of
this Commonwealth . [ Acts 1912 , p . 147. ]
SEC . 576c .
3. How agreement to purchase acknowledged . A copy of the agree-
ment to purchase and sell shall be acknowledged by a majority of the Board
of Directors of the purchasing corporation and shall be recorded in the
same manner as is now provided for amendments to articles of incorpora-
tion , in the counties where the corporations have , their legal domicile .
[Acts 1912 , p . 148. ]
The act became effective from approval by Governor , March 11, 1912 .

SEC . 602a .
DEPARTMENT OF BANKING .
AN ACT to establish a Department of Banking , providing for the appointment of a
commissioner , deputy commissioner and examiners thereof and prescribing
their duties ; and for the examination of all financial institutions organized
and doing business under the laws of this Commonwealth .
[ Act March 1, 1912. Acts 1912 , Chap . 4 , p . 8. ]
99
1. Department of Banking created . There is hereby established a
department to be designated " Department of Banking , which shall be
charged with the enforcement of all laws heretofore passed , or which
may hereafter be passed , relating to banks , trust companies , saving
banks , combined banks , and combined banks and trust companies , organ-
ized and doing business under the laws of the Commonwealth of Ken-
tucky. Unless otherwise stated the words " bank " or " banks " herein
used shall include all banks , trust companies , savings banks , combined
banks , and combined banks and trust companies . [ Acts 1912 , p . 8. ]
SEC . 602b .
2. Banking Commissioner . The chief officer of this department shall
be designated " Banking Commissioner " of the Commonwealth of Kentucky .
The Governor of Kentucky shall appoint , during the month of June , 1912 ,
and every four years thereafter a Banking Commissioner , under this
Act , whose term of office shall begin the first day of July succeeding
his appointment , and he shall hold office for the term of four years and
until a successor is appointed and qualified . The Banking Commissioner
shall perform the duties hereinafter described , and shall appoint to ,
remove from , and fill any vacancies in all offices in the Department of
Banking . He may adopt such regulations and forms as may be necessary
and proper , under this Act . He shall keep his office , which shall be pro-
vided and furnished by the Commonwealth , at the seat of Government ,
and shall receive for his services the sum of three thousand six hundred
dollars ( $3,600 ) per annum , payable monthly , out of the State Treasury .
The Banking Commissioner and his deputy shall be allowed their neces-
sary traveling and other expenses of conducting the office , payable on
properly itemized and verified accounts filed with and approved by the
Auditor of the State of Kentucky . [ Acts 1912 , p . 9. ]

7. Qualifications . No Banking Commissioner , Deputy Banking Com-
missioner , or State Bank Examiner , shall be or become indebted , directly
or indirectly , either as borrower , indorser, surety or guarantor , to any
bank under his supervision , or subject to his examination ; nor shall he be
a director , officer or employe in any such bank , but no person shall be
appointed to examine the affairs of any bank or trust company in any
county in which he holds stock in either a State or a National bank .
If any officer become so indebted to , or so interested in , any such bank
or shall engage or become interested in the sale of securities as a busi-
ness , or in the negotiation of loans for others , his office shall , ipso facto ,
become vacant . The Cashier or President of any bank to which any of
said officers shall become indebted , shall make immediate report thereof
to the Governor , who shall remove the officer so offending .
Every Banking Commissioner , Deputy Banking Commissioner and
State Bank Examiner shall be a resident and citizen of the Commonwealth
of Kentucky , shall be a practical bookkeeper and accountant and shall
have had not less than four years actual experience as officer or clerk in
a bank or trust company , and shall take the oath required of officers by
the Constitution and laws of this Commonwealth , for the faithful per-
formance of his duties . They shall severally execute bond with good
surety , to be approved by the Auditor , for the faithful performance of
their duties . The bond of the Banking Commissioner shall be in the penal
sum of fifty thousand dollars ( $50,000 ) ; the bond of the Deputy Banking
Commissioner shall be in the penal sum of twenty -five thousand dollars.
( $25,000 ) ; the bond of each State Bank Examiner shall be in the penal
sum of ten thousand dollars ( $ 10,000 ) . All bonds so required to be exe-
cuted shall be filed as part of the public records in the office of the Secre-
tary of State . The cost of all contingency and all bonds required to be
given under this section , shall be borne and paid by the State in the
same manner as other expenses of the department . [Acts 1912 , p . 11. ]
SEC . 602h .
8. Inspection of banks . Every bank organized and doing business
under the laws of this State shall be subject to the inspection of the Bank-
ing Commissioner . Such Commissioner shall personally or by the Deputy
Commissioner or a State Bank Examiner , visit each bank and examine
the cash , bills , collateral securities , other assets , books of account , and all
other papers and books of such bank . On such examination , inquiry

the investment and disposition of its funds , the safety and prudence of

are held , and whether the requirements of its charter and of the laws of
this State have been complied with in the administration of its affairs ,
and as to such other matters as the Commissioners may deem necessary .
Such examination shall be made of every bank , at least once in every
year, but not to exceed twice in any one year , unless it shall appear
from examination or from the report or reports of a bank that such bank
has failed to comply with the laws relating to banks, or a regulation of
the Department of Banking .
The Banking Commissioner , Deputy Banking Commissioner , and every
State Bank Examiner , shall have the power to administer an oath to any
person whose testimony may be required in the examination of any

intended examination shall be given to the bank to be examined until
the examining officer is prepared to proceed immediately with the exam-
ination . No officer or employee of the Banking Department nor the
examiner conducting any examination , shall impart any information ob-
tained by him during such examination , except so far as may be neces-
sary in the performance of is official duty as provided by law.
The Bank Commissioner shall prescribe , from time to time , the order
in which such banks shall be examined , but no such bank shall be
examined twice in succession by the same Examiner unless directed by
the Commissioner . [ Acts 1912 , p . 12. ]

13. Penalties . If the Deputy Banking Commissioner , or any State

16. When banks in unsafe condition- Commissioner to take charge .
If from any examination made as provided in this Act , it shall appear
that any bank is insolvent or that its capital has become impaired , and
is permitted to remain impaired beyond the period allowed by law , it
shall be the duty of the Banking Commissioner in person or by his Deputy
or by a State Bank Examiner immediately to take charge of such bank
and all property and effects thereof .
If an Examiner shall find that any bank is pursuing a dangerous and
unsafe policy , the Examiner shall call the directors and officers of such
institution together and advise them fully of the nature of such objection-
able practices , and warn them against a repetition thereof , and shall make
a full report to the Banking Commissioner of the practices warned against ,
and the advice given by him, and thereupon the Banking Commissioner ,
if he deem it proper , shall , in person or by written notice to each director ,
require an abandonment or cessation of such objectionable practices or
policy , and if his directions are not complied with , he may place a State
Bank Examiner in charge of such bank , or he may adopt such other
policy as may in his judgment seem wise and best calculated to bring the
institution back to a safe condition . The officers , directors , or stock-
holders of any bank shall have the right forthwith , upon his declaring
his intention of doing so , to execute to such Commissioner a bond with
surety or security approved by him, conditioned to secure the creditors
of such bank , and upon the execution of such bond the Banking Com-
missioner shall leave with , or restore the custody and management of
such bank to the officers and directors thereof . The Commissioner may ,
if he deem necessary , cause a petition to be filed in the Circuit Court
of the county where such bank is located , and apply to such court
or to the Judge thereof when the court is not in session , for the appoint-
ment of a receiver of such bank , and thereupon such court or the Judge
thereof shall set a date for the hearing of the application for the appoint-
ment of a receiver , not later than twenty days from the date of such
motion is made and of which notice shall be served upon the bank . Upon
such hearing the parties may be heard by affidavits or upon oral exam-
ination in court or before the Judge and thereupon the Judge shall hear
and determine the question of the appointment of such receiver , and if
the court shall determine that such action or proposed action of the
Commissioner was justified , the court shall appoint a receiver , and shall
fix the amount of the bond to be given by him . [ Acts 1912 , p . 20. ]

SEC . 617. CORPORATION LAWS .
SEC . 616d .
CONSOLIDATION OF TRUST COMPANIES .
AN ACT to provide for the consolidation of Trust Companies organized under the
laws of the State of Kentucky .
[ Act March 12, 1912. Acts 1912 , Chap . 41 , p . 178. ]
1. Trust companies authorized to consolidate -resulting company ob-
ligated to perform all duties and carry out all liabilities of constituent
companies . Any two or more corporations organized under the laws of
this State , for the purpose of conducting the business of trust companies ,
may consolidate their capital stock , assets and management into one
organization . The separate existence of each corporation shall continue
and all duties , powers and discretions of the constituent companies as
personal representative , trustee , assignee , guardian , agent or otherwise
conferred , shall be imposed upon and may be exercised by the consolidated
corporation ; and such duty , power or discretion , at the time of consoli-
dation or thereafter imposed upon either of the constituent companies , may
be performed or exercised by the consolidated corporation in its own name.
or in the name of the constituent company upon which was imposed or
conferred such duty , power , or discretion ; or by the constituent com-
pany upon which was imposed or conferred such duty, power or discre-
tion ; but in every case the consolidated corporation shall be liable for
the proper performance of such duty and the proper exercise of such
power or discretion . [ Acts 1912 , p . 178. ]
SEC . 616e .
2. Continued existence of constituent corporations -directorate . The
method and effect of such consolidation shall be as now provided by Sec-
tions 555 , 555a , 556 , 557 and 558 of Chapter 32 , Kentucky Statutes , ex-
cept that as above provided , the separate existence of the constituent
corporations shall not cease , and the consolidated corporation and the
constituent corporations shall continue to exist , the management of said
cosolidated corporation and each of said constituent corporations being in
the directors and officers of the consolidated corporation . [ Acts 1912 ,
p. 178. ]
SEC . 616f .
3. Emergency clause . Whereas , much doubt exists as to the effect
of a consolidation , under the present law , of companies organized to
conduct the business of trust companies , and such doubt is interfering
with such consolidation , therefore , an emergency is declared to exist ,
and this Act shall take effect from and after its passage . [Acts 1912 ,
p . 179. ]

1. Investigation of fires by Insurance Commissioner , Fire Marshal ,
assistants and chief fire department -statements -records- (for Fire
Marshal's appointment , see Section 762g ) . The Insurance Commissioner ,
the Fire Marshal and his assistants hereinafter provided for , the chief of
the fire department or chief of police ( where no chief of fire department )
in cities and towns , and the sheriff of the county where such fires occur
or conditions exist , outside of incorporated cities or towns , are hereby
authorized to investigate the cause , origin and circumstances of every fire
occurring in such cities or towns or counties in which property has been
destroyed or damaged , and where conditions exist which might cause fire ,
and may make investigation whether such fires or conditions were or are
the result of carelessness or design . A preliminary investigation may be
made by the chief of fire department or the chief of police (where no
chief of fire department ) in incorporated cities and towns , and by the
sheriff of the county where such fires occur or conditions exist outside of
an incorporated city or town , which shall be begun in three days , not
including Sundays , of the occurrence of such fires , and the Insurance
Commissioner , the Fire Marshal and his assistants , or any of them , shall
have the right to supervise and direct such investigation whenever he or
they deem it expedient or necessary . The officer other than the Insurance
Commissioner making such investigation of fires or conditions shall forth-
with notify the Insurance Commissioner and shall , within thirty days
after the occurrence of a fire , investigate it and furnish to the said Insur

ance Commissioner or the Fire Marshal a written statement of all the
facts relating to the cause and origin of the fire , the kind , value and
ownership of the property destroyed , and such oher information as may

the Fire Marshal . (The Fire Marshal shall keep in his office a record of
all fires occurring in the State , together with all facts , statistics and cir-
cumstances including the origin of the fires and existing conditions which.
may be determined by the investigation provided for by this Act ; such
record shall at all times be open to public inspection . ) [ Acts 1912 , p . 105. ]

the testimony on oath of all persons supposed to be cognizant of any

Corporation Laws Continued .
RAILROAD COMPANIES .

incorporation under this section ; but the Court intimates that the incorporation in

ship nor deprive it of any rights it enjoys as a foreign railway corporation . Plummer

has not complied with this statute is of no effect in a controversy between the

SEC . 768 .
( 1) Under subsection 4 of this section the right to condemn is not confined to
the land absolutely required at the time of taking , but extends to so much as the
present plans and purposes of the railroad company show will be reasonably necessary .

( 2 ) A railroad company is liable to indictment for suffering a bridge , part of
its right of way , to remain out of repair , although the bridge had been built and
maintained by the town across a street on which the bridge was located . Ill . Cent .
R. Co. v. Com., 138 Ky . 742 , 129 S. W. 94 .
(3 ) A railroad company which constructs its road across a highway must restore
the highway as near as may be to its former condition , although it may be necessary

for this purcose to go out on the highway beyond its right of way in building the

regard for the interest of both the parties . Chesapeake & Ohio Railway Company v .
Herringer , 158 Ky . 267 , 164 S. W. 948 .
As the railroad company could not build the crossing until the place where it was
to be built was fixed , no action lies against it for damages until the location of the

(7) For form of petition under this section , see Kentucky Form Book , Form

precedent to the occupation of its streets by a steam railroad . City of Covington v .
L. & N. R. Co. , 158 Ky. 136 , 164 S. W. 329 .
A railroad company can not construct its line across a street or sidewalk without

lawfully obstruct the highway by trains for a longer time than five minutes , as

SEC . 820b .
TWO AND A HALF CENTS PER MILE LIMIT OF PASSENGER
CHARGE FOR CERTAIN COMMON CARRIERS .
[ This Act was held invalid for the reason that it did not contain an enacting
clause as provided by Ky. Const . Sec . 62. Com. v . I. C. R. Co. , 160 Ky. 745. ]
[ Act March 20 , 1914. Acts 1914 , Chap . 68 , p , 176. ]
1. Railroads-transportation of passengers-two and a half cents per
mile limit of charge . That it shall hereafter be unlawful for any common
carrier earning as much or more than $4,000.00 per year per mile gross ,
from all sources on its said road , and engaged in the carriage of passengers
upon a railroad or railroads , between points in this State , to charge in
excess of two and one-half cents per mile for the carriage of an adult
passenger . Passengers , however , over five and under twelve years of age ,
shall be charged one-half of the adults fares ; adding sufficient , when
neccessary to make the fares end in naught or five . Provided , That the
minimum charge in no case shall be less than ten cents , and in deter-
mining the charge , fractions of less than one -half mile shall be disregarded ,
and all other fractions counted as one mile ; and for an odd number of
miles , the carrier may charge as for the next highest even number of miles .
Provided , that where any passenger is given an opportunity , for thirty
minutes continuously before the departure of any train , to secure a ticket
entitling him to carriage , and fails to do so , then such carrier may charge
and collect in addition to the regular ticket rates , the fixed sum of ten
cents from all cash fare passengers . And provided further , that any person
applying therefor , the said common carrier earning as much or more than
$4,000.00 per year per mile gross , from all sources on its said road , shall
issue to such person a mileage book of one thousand miles , or multiples
195

SEC . 820f . CORPORATION LAWS .
thereof , at the price of two cents per mile , which mileage book shall be
inter- changeable with all other railroads of the Commonwealth earning a
like amount , subject to such regulations as may be prescribed by the Rail-
road Commission to insure payment to the company honoring such mileage
from the company issuing such mileage . [ Acts 1914 , p . 176. ]
SEC . 820c .
2. Personal baggage to be carried - limit . That each common carrier
in this State which shall engage in the carriage of passengers by railroad
between points in this State , shall receive and transport with each pas-
senger tendering the same , the personal baggage of such passenger , not
exceeding one hundred and fifty pounds for adult and seventy -five pounds
for a minor less than twelve years old , and such personal baggage shall be
carried without compensation other than the passenger transportation
charge . All baggage as defined by this Act in excess of the weight here
specified is hereby declared to be excess baggage , and such carriers are
required to carry such excess baggage for the passenger , as required by this
Act . Provided further , that such carrier shall be required to carry bag-
gage only on trains equipped with a baggage car . [ Acts 1914 , p . 177. ]
SEC . 820d .
3. Drummers ' samples are baggage . The samples , goods , wares , ap-
pliances and catalogues of commercial travelers or their employers , and
used by them for the purpose of transacting their business , and carried
with them solely for that purpose , when securely packed and locked in
substantial trunks or sample cases of convenient shapes and weight for
handling , are hereby declared to be baggage within the meaning of this
Act , and such carriers are required to transport the same with the pas-
sengers as required by this Act . [ Acts 1914 , p . 178. ]
SEC . 820e .
4. Charge for excess baggage . Excess baggage is to be charged for
on a basis of 16 2-3 per centum of the adult passenger fare per hundred
pounds . Provided , That no charge for such excess shall be less than
twenty-five cents when the entire baggage is less than five hundred pounds ,
or less than fifty cents when the entire baggage is over five hundred pounds ,
and in determining the rate , fractions of less than one mile shall be dis-
regarded , and fractions of one-half or more shall be counted as one mile .
[Acts 1914 , p . 178. ]
SEC . 8201.
5. Penalties for violations . Any common carrier violating any pro-
visions or requirement of this Act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and
upon conviction thereof shall be fined not less than twenty -five nor more
than one hundred dollars in any court of competent jurisdiction , in any
county into or through which the line or lines of railroad of the offending

railroad or branch line less than fifty miles in length . [ Acts 1914 , p . 178. ]

such samples , goods , wares , appliances or catalogues of any commercial
traveler or his employer , the carrier shall not be liable for any greater
proportion of the value thereof or the damages sustained thereto than the
excess baggage fare paid by the passenger bears to the current rate of
freight on such line for like articles in like packages between the same
points. [ Acts 1914 , p . 179. ] .

2. Board of Commissioners appointed . A Board of Commissioners is

SEC . 921C .
3. Commission to select temporary county seat , etc. to report . The
said Commission shall have power , and it shall be its duty , to select a
temporary seat of government for said county , and to provide temporary
places for holding the court and courts in said county , and for keeping
the public records of said county until a permanent seat of government.
is selected , and as hereinafter provided . It shall also have the power , and
it shall be its duty , to divide said county into six magisterial districts .
For this purpose they will meet at the town of Pine Knot , as soon after

and impartially divide said county into said magisterial districts .
They will give the boundary of each district laid off by them ; they
will also divide said county into voting precincts , and fix and select the
voting places in each of said precincts . They will make up in writing a
report of their acts and doings under this Act and forward one copy to
the Secretary of State and one copy they will retain and will deposit with
the County Court Clerk of said county as soon as one is appointed and

and spread it of record upon the order book of his office . [ Acts 1912 , pp .
188 , 189. ]
